purpose: Review evidence and implemented asset provenance for the SPEC.md rebuild of the Inclusão Digital UEMG portal.

generator.configuredProvider: configured image provider (Azure OpenAI v1 compatible)
generator.credentialsHandling: Credential read from the environment by the tool; never printed, logged, or committed

infrastructureReceipt.observation: Dated observation on 2026-08-16 (a measured window, not a permanent guarantee): with Azure OpenAI v1 / gpt-image-2, image_generate at quality=low completed in every measured attempt, while quality=medium and quality=high returned a transport-layer network timeout in the measured attempts below. The configured endpoint answered HTTP 200 during the same window, so the base connection was healthy.

measurements_2026-08-16.high_1536x864: 0/4 succeeded (network timeout); attempts that also passed a reference image failed, and the tec-image helper documents that this path does not accept a reference image for image-to-image

infrastructureReceipt.decision: Selected assets were generated at quality=low, which for gpt-image-2 still yields clean, review-grade output. Production finals may be re-rendered at a higher quality later, or via a queue/retry path. Recorded here as the receipt behind the quality choice.

world.name: Ateliê de Autonomia
world.oneLine: A calm hand-cut-paper craft world set between a Brazilian public-university lab and the learner's own home, where older adults are shown as capable protagonists, never as helpless.
world.replaces: Colcha de Retalhos (chita quilt) - see SPEC.md section 4 for why.

freezeList.camera: seated eye level, wide contextual scenes; no forced perspective, no top-down
freezeList.lighting: clear warm daylight (late morning to afternoon)
freezeList.people: Brazilian adults aged 60-75, varied skin tones and genders, dignified everyday clothing, attentive and capable expressions; monitors read as equals
freezeList.environment: Brazilian public-university computer laboratory in Frutal and the learner's home living room/kitchen
freezeList.deviceLanguage: recognizable hardware shells with blank pale geometric screens; all real UI stays HTML/CSS/SVG
